data.summary:
Tested the DVWA brute force endpoint (low security). The login form uses GET method with username/password parameters and has no rate limiting, no CAPTCHA, no account lockout. Clear response differentiation exists: failed login returns '

Username and/or password incorrect.
' while successful login returns '

Welcome to the password protected area {username}

'. Brute force enumeration discovered 3 valid user credentials: gordonb:abc123, pablo:letmein, smithy:password. The source code confirms direct GET parameter usage with no protection mechanisms. The help page explicitly states 'The developer has completely missed out any protections methods'.

candidates.title: Brute Force - No Rate Limiting on Login Form
candidates.claim: The login form has no rate limiting, no CAPTCHA, and no account lockout, enabling unlimited password guessing. Attackers can enumerate valid credentials via the clear success/failure response differentiation.
candidates.proof_excerpt:
session response body diff: failed='

Username and/or password incorrect.
' vs success='

Welcome to the password protected area gordonb

'
candidates.poc_hint: 1. Send GET request to http://127.0.0.1:8080/vulnerabilities/brute/?username=USER&password=PASS&Login=Login with valid session cookies. 2. Check response body: if it contains 'Welcome to the password protected area' the credentials are valid; if 'Username and/or password incorrect.' they are invalid. 3. No delay or lockout observed after many rapid requests. 4. Example found: gordonb:abc123 returns 'Welcome to the password protected area gordonb' while nonexistent:wrong returns 'Username and/or password incorrect.'

candidates.title: Credentials Discovered via Brute Force
candidates.claim: Valid user credentials were enumerated through brute force testing against the unprotected login form.
candidates.proof_excerpt: Brute force script output: 'SUCCESS: gordonb:abc123 (displayed: gordonb)\nSUCCESS: pablo:letmein (displayed: pablo)\nSUCCESS: smithy:password (displayed: smithy)'
candidates.poc_hint: Run automated script testing common username/password pairs against the endpoint. Each success returns 'Welcome to the password protected area USERNAME' in the response body. Discovered: gordonb:abc123, pablo:letmein, smithy:password. Total: 3 valid credentials found from ~200 attempts.

facts.summary: Brute force endpoint has no rate limiting, no CAPTCHA, no account lockout at low security level
Found 3 valid user credentials via brute force: gordonb:abc123, pablo:letmein, smithy:password
Clear success/failure response differentiation enables automated brute force

deadends: Admin password not found with tested wordlist (password, admin, 123456, letmein, root, admin123, etc.)
No SQL injection tested as separate finding; focus was on brute force enumeration only
